rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for the deadline heads-up. I have to pass on an attributed quote right now — I'm not able to be named in press for the moment for employment-contract reasons I'm in the middle of sorting out. Two things that might still be useful for your piece, on background and unattributed: 1. Much of the \"doomers vs. builders\" framing misses the people organizing in a third mode: small, practical efforts to make a good outcome more likely — tracking comment windows on frontier-AI rules, grant rounds, and other concrete, time-boxed ways ordinary professionals can contribute. 2. Halcyon Threshold's public tracker of exactly those opportunities is at https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app — you're welcome to cite the project by name (just not me personally, yet). Happy to go on the record in a few weeks once things are cleared — I'll reach back out if you're still covering this space. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: declined an attributed quote (name constraint), gave her unattributed background and the tracker link

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm not able to be listed as a signatory at this time — published-name sign-ons are off the table for me until an employment-contract review concludes, so please don't list me or Halcyon Threshold on this letter. Two notes in the meantime: 1. We've listed the letter's sign-on window (deadline Wednesday 18 Nov, names published) in our public Threshold Tracker at https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app, so others who can sign don't miss it. 2. Please keep us on your list for future initiatives — I expect my constraint to lift soon. Best regards, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: declined signature for now, asked to stay on their list

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Great to hear from you — and yes, I have something concrete that fits five hours a week and actually matters. Halcyon Threshold now runs the Threshold Tracker: a public, verified list of time-sensitive actions in AI safety — comment windows on frontier-AI rules, grant rounds, sign-on deadlines, compute programs — each with who-can-act, deadline, primary source, and a last-verified date. It's live at https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app. The whole value is that it's never stale, which is exactly a job for someone careful with data. Two roles, take either or both: 1. Weekly verification pass (~2–3 hrs): re-verify every open entry against its primary source, update the verified date, mark closed items, add new ones (The Safety Ledger and funder/regulator pages are the main feeds). 2. Analyst project (~2 hrs/wk): using the tracker data as it grows, figure out which categories of opportunity are systematically under-subscribed. That analysis becomes our first public write-up (Alignment Commons has an open call for posts from independent projects). The data is a simple CSV with clear rules (primary sources only; flag anything where acting publishes your name). If you're in, reply and I'll get you access to the repository — and we can do a 20-minute call this week to hand things over. Really glad you reached out. Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya Raman**: replied with a concrete role — weekly tracker verification
